text:
Recent work supports testing richer negatives and ranking objectives while retaining NextItNet. [Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)](https://dspace.mit.edu/entities/publication/5392aca9-0bae-4176-9b3a-a8165957ba26) approximates catalog softmax using GPU-efficient maximum-inner-product retrieval of informative items. [Correcting the LogQ Correction (RecSys 2025)](https://github.com/NonameUntitled/logq/) provides implementations comparing uniform, in-batch and mixed negatives with alternative sampling corrections. These motivate multiple-negative cross-entropy, but correction must match the actual sampling procedure; deterministic hard-negative selection should not be treated as uniform sampling.

For ranking alignment, [Improved Estimation of Ranks (2024)](https://research.google/pubs/improved-estimation-of-ranks-for-learning-item-recommenders-with-negative-sampling/) shows that correcting sampled rank estimates improves sampled WARP/LambdaRank training. [SoftmaxLoss@K (KDD 2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05673) uses quantiles to model top-K truncation and a smooth NDCG@K surrogate. Neither establishes gains on this benchmark’s sampled HR@10. A [2026 preprint](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.11061) also cautions against assuming more negatives always help: under its fixed-memory assumptions and experiments, allocating more capacity to batch size performs better.

Practical hypothesis: score a modest random candidate pool using the current NextItNet, retain a mixture of random and moderately hard negatives, and gradually increase hardness. Exclude padding, targets and known training positives; deduplicate candidates. Treat extreme hardness as uncertain rather than proof of irrelevance: earlier [UFNRec research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2208.04116) explicitly identifies false negatives as a sequential-recommendation problem. Downweighting suspicious candidates is a proposed safeguard, not established evidence of benefit here. Compare uniform multi-negative softmax against this mining variant using the fixed macro validation HR@10; retain one trained model per category.
